title: Translate a data-layer SQLException at the service boundary

blocks.text: A service should not leak its data layer's `SQLException`. Translate it at the boundary into an exception of the service's own level of abstraction, keeping it as the cause.

items: Complete the checked `OrderLookupException(String message, Throwable cause)`.

Write `OrderService(OrderDao dao)` and `String findOrder(long id) throws OrderLookupException`, which returns `dao.load(id)`. When `load` throws `SQLException`, throw `OrderLookupException("Could not load order <id>")`.

blocks.text: A caller depends only on the service's API, yet an operator reading the log still needs to see `Caused by: java.sql.SQLException`. Catch only what you can translate.

cases.says: An order the DAO loads is returned.
A SQLException from the DAO leaves the service as OrderLookupException("Could not load order <id>").
The SQLException is kept as the cause, so the real reason still shows in the logs.
Only the SQLException is caught; an unchecked exception from the DAO is a bug and propagates as it is.

concepts: Catching Exception also catches the RuntimeExceptions that signal bugs, so catch only what you can handle.
A layer translates a lower-level exception into its own, keeping the original as the cause.
